items.title: Teacher-Agnostic Temporal Knowledge Distillation for Resource-Efficient Sound Event Detection
items.authors: Gihun Son(Hanyang University); Pil Moo Byun(Hanyang University); Joon-Hyuk Chang(Hanyang University)
items.abstract: Sound event detection (SED) needs frame-level detection, yet recent work has focused on high-capacity models, leaving resource-efficient SED relatively underexplored. We propose teacher-agnostic temporal knowledge distillation (TAT-KD), a knowledge distillation (KD) framework for SED that distills from any teacher architecture by using teacher logits as a common distillation space. To transfer temporal context, we introduce a conformer-based temporal context projector that models temporal dependencies during projection and a teacher-confidence-aware distillation loss that downweights ambiguous outputs via normalized confidence weights. On the domestic environment sound event detection benchmark, TAT-KD outperformed training from scratch and logit-/feature-based KD, achieving polyphonic sound detection score of 0.574 with 4.548M parameters and 3.668G multiply-accumulate operations, showing competitive performance with far fewer parameters and computations than state-of-the-art models.

items.title: A Sensitivity Analysis of Multi-Event Audio Grounding in Audio LLMs
items.authors: Taehan Lee(Sogang University); Jaehan Jung(Sogang University); Hyukjun Lee(Sogang University)
items.abstract: Audio LLMs have shown a strong ability to understand audio samples, yet their reliability in complex acoustic scenes remains under-explored. Unlike prior work limited to small scale or less controlled query construction, we present a large-scale evaluation of event grounding and false alarms as auditory scene complexity increases. Using 71K AudioCapsV2 clips, we extract normalized (source, attribute) events and build two query types: present-event queries for ground-truth detection and absent-event queries to probe hallucinations, using similarity-filtered negative sampling in an audio-aligned text embedding space. We evaluate four SOTA Audio LLMs with 12 prompt variants over 500K yes/no queries per model. Across models, increasing event count consistently lowers true-positive rate and raises false-positive rate, while prompts induce a strong trade-off between the two. Our confidence analysis shows that models become more uncertain on multi-event audio, revealing room for improvement.

items.title: RAISE: Resolving Ambiguity in Audio Understanding with Imagination and Selective Extraction
items.authors: Yueqian Lin(Duke University); Qinsi Wang(Duke University); Yudong Liu(Duke University); Hancheng Ye(Duke University); Hai Li(Duke University); Yiran Chen(Duke University)
items.abstract: Audio Large Language Models (Audio LLMs) are prone to perceptual hallucination under acoustic interference or fine-grained ambiguity. Robust auditory understanding demands active verification: even state-of-the-art reasoning models hallucinate when forced to decode ambiguous internal representations. We introduce RAISE (Resolving Ambiguity with Imagination and Selective Extraction), a training-free framework that equips Audio LLMs with two cognitively motivated listening strategies. Selective Extraction isolates target signals from noise; Auditory Imagination synthesizes candidate references for comparative reasoning. Instead of relying on ambiguous internal representations, the model grounds every prediction in explicit acoustic evidence. On two challenging benchmarks, MMAR and MMAU, RAISE delivers consistent gains of up to 12.4% without any parameter updates.

items.title: The silence of the weights: a structural pruning strategy for Attention-based audio signal architectures with second-order metrics
items.authors: Andrea Diecidue(Politecnico di Milano); Carlo Alberto Barbano(University of Turin); Piero Fraternali(Politecnico di Milano); Mathieu Fontaine(Institut Polytechnique de Paris); Enzo Tartaglione(Institut Polytechnique de Paris)
items.abstract: Transformer-based models have become the state of the art across multiple domains, from natural language processing to machine listening, enabled by the attention mechanisms. However, the attention layers require a large number of parameters and high-end hardware for both training and inference. We propose a novel channel-pruning technique explicitly targeted at the attention mechanism, decoupling the pruning of each head and the four matrices in the attention block: query, key, value, and output projection matrices, employing a second-order metric to score the network's parameters. We compare our technique against head-pruning strategies and magnitude-driven scoring metrics, investigating the effects of pruning on Audio Spectrogram Transformer (AST) and Whisper. Our results show that even after pruning 50% of the parameters in the attention block, performance is largely preserved. The code is available on GitHub.

items.title: Trajectory Variance: An Unsupervised Measure of Developmental Vocal Plasticity in Birdsong
items.authors: Kanghwi Lee(ETH Zurich; University of Zurich)
items.abstract: How much does a vocalization change over the course of development? We propose trajectory variance, a per-vocalization plasticity score that answers this question without type labels. A displacement model learns to predict age-conditioned shifts in autoencoder latent space; the variance of its predictions across target ages quantifies how much each vocalization would change if produced at different developmental stages. Evaluated on three zebra finches (183K-274K vocalizations, 40-101 days post-hatch), trajectory variance separates learned song syllables from innate calls (Cohen's d = 0.29-0.57, AUC = 0.58-0.67, after controlling for duration), while no nonparametric baseline achieves consistent separation. Trajectory variance also correlates with spectral flatness across all three birds (r = -0.48 to -0.75): more plastic vocalizations tend to have more tonal, structured spectra.

items.title: Beyond Uncertainty and Diversity: Temporal-Spectral Guided Active Learning for Audio
items.authors: Hui Geng(National University of Defense Technology); Tianjiao Wan(National University of Defense Technology); Yi Su(National University of Defense Technology); Qisheng Xu(National University of Defense Technology); Hengzhu Liu(National University of Defense Technology); Kele Xu(National University of Defense Technology)
items.abstract: Active Learning (AL) holds significant potential to reduce annotation costs for audio signal processing tasks under supervised finetuning by strategically selecting informative unlabeled samples for labeling. However, existing AL methods typically rely on general selection criteria such as uncertainty or representativeness, which fail to account for the intricate temporal-spectral structures inherent in audio signals. These structures play a critical role in determining sample informativeness, making direct application of existing AL approaches suboptimal for audio tasks. To address this limitation, we propose a novel AL framework for audio, named Temporal-Spectral Active Learning (TSAL), explicitly bridging the gap between model optimization and audio characteristics. Since temporal-spectral patterns cannot be directly extracted or explicitly defined, TSAL constructs these informative patterns by modeling the soft-loss distribution. Furthermore, it incorporates feature-gradient similarity to guide the selection of unlabeled samples that exhibit these distinctive patterns. Extensive experiments on several audio benchmarks demonstrate that TSAL consistently out-performs state-of-the-art AL methods, significantly improving sampling efficiency and effectiveness under limited annotation budgets, while highlighting the importance of temporal-spectral guidance for advancing audio AL.
